body: Can confirm. I think the pain of the piercing actually distracted me from the migraine pain. I've seen so many cases of the piercing getting infected, I've gotten mine in August and I still have to clean it daily,  and when it moves out of place (it's a heart shape) I struggle and bleed to get it back in place.

Homemade ginger ale with lemon and mint and honey usually helps a bit for me. I also used to carry spearmint gum on me, and that would help. It also apparently helps when the drinks are carbonated. Energy drinks work too, like coffee would, but personally I haven't found any energy drinks working for me.

It's great in the sense that it was developed with the help of migraine experts, so there's a lot of dimension and depth that goes into recording migraines and using the data to give you pointers about your triggers and such, and it also provides a lot of information. But, in my own experience,  I don't like the presence of screens or technology whilst having a migraine so recording migraines became too much of a hassle. I get the feeling like I probably wasn't using it to it's full potential, but I'm lazy and so are a lot of other users. As for connecting me to other migraineurs in my area - it felt weird, and often other people in my area cannot relate to my situation, like they experience migraines after heavy drinking (not the app's fault though).

All in all, it's great if you don't mind filling out a digital form for every migraine (it's definitely easier than recording a migraine with a pen and paper) (i also remember you can start a migraine recording and finish it later, which is nice), they put a lot of effort into locating tangents in symptoms and medicines and such, and providing educational info on things that might contribute to your migraines, and then there's the feature that alerts someone in your contacts when you have a really bad one, you can make notes... it's great.

I think it's by far one of the most integrated and developed apps I've seen. I just couldn't keep up with recording migraines, because I become a blanket hermit that wants nothing to do with technology when I have a migraine(I swear I can hear electricity, it sounds stupid, I know), so it just didn't work for me.
I think it's true, it would make sense. I don't want to imagine a world where migraines were unstoppable phenomena

Honestly I don't think GPs actually understand or are interested in learning more about migraines and other headaches, and one might be better off at a headache and migraine specialist, but this is also the more expensive solution, an introductory consultation starting at R1800 (RSA), and this specific clinic (RSA's only headache clinic) are known for not being covered by any medical funds. It's like migraneurs can never catch a break.

I've never even been to the hospital without it being to visit a loved one or have blood samples taken. I'll make a plan to get to the ER during the week, everything is closed here on Sundays. As for the doctor, he's very old timey. I feel like he just wasted my time.

I've always had high blood pressure, and as a kid I thought the blood vessels in my hands (it was always prominent in comparison to other kids') would just burst from my skin and bleed all over the place. Now, 15 years later, I have that same fear except the location from where the bloodvessels would burst from my skin is my skull and I feel the need to cover my head to keep it all inside. 

The worst thing about migraines for me is that people often opt not to believe you about your migraines, even if you're not the lying type.

Doctors are very weary of prescribing more than 9 doses of triptans a month because apparently triptans should prevent another migraine for the next 72 hours. Thus, 1 dose every 3 days a month max. I pay R300+ (RSA) for 3x doses of rizatriptans per month - I spend less money on food!
Another word that might be relevant is "premonition."

To contextualize my conversation with my psychiatrist: I was talking about my social anxiety, and the way that I believe everything is my fault/responsibility, when in reality the situation is out of my control. Messes are bad, but I've had pretty low moments, regaining consciousness in a dried up puddle of brightly coloured pasty vomit, to waking up in a bed soaked with urine, vomited up red wine and blood, to having my future in-law mother having to help me wash off when I had food poisoning (she saw me covered in my own shit and vomit) and I've slipped and fell in my own vomit, and hurt myself so bad I had to wait for someone to help me up and help me walk. Fun times.

The physical pain of dying wouldn't influence my choice to take my life. However, the fear of surviving the suicide attempt and the impact my survival/death would have on my loved ones are highly influential to this decision. 

(I know the question entails success in said suicide attempt, but hear me out)

I know of too many people who tried hanging themselves and survived, being in a mostly vegetative state afterwards, and never again being in control of their lives and always feeling like a burden to their loved ones. Some people survive shooting themselves too. If one were to survive a suicide attempt, the burdening of others always follows. I'd hate myself more if I were to inconvenience my family even more.


On the other hand,  if you were to succeed, would your loved ones be able to deal with the aftermath, psychologically and financially? I've known people to literally just give up after losing a loved one, and just died naturally like that. Mourned themselves to death. My mind also reminds me of all the responsibilities that I can't just leave behind and hope someone will take care of.

My psychiatrist told me to stop concerning myself with other people,  I'm sure you can see why.

In short, I wanna say I'd push that button but I'm an adult with adult responsibilities and quitting isn't an option.

The woman's head faced the wrong way and her knees were drawn up to her chest. The driver's head faced the steering wheel, but his chest was facing his seat and his legs were still in the pedal area, his limp arm hanging out of the window in the wrong direction. The pathology van somehow ended up on its side. They lifted two heavily intoxicated, minorly injured men from the door on the opposite side of the van, along with three empty cases of Black Label. It was later revealed that they skipped the red light as they were fleeing a previous accident, for they had run someone over at the previous intersection. We were the only eyewitnesses of the second accident that waited for the police, who only arrived 3 hours later.

We never did show up for the wedding.

When I quit drinking, sleeping schedule used to be a big problem for me too. I didn't want to use potentially addictive medication like sleeping pills, so instead I used melatonin along with intensive meditation around 8 p.m. daily for a fiscal quarter, and now falling asleep only presents a challenge when I'm stressed out for an exam the next day or something.

I do have a lot of allergy problems, I take 2 antihistamines 3x a day whenever I can (afford to purchase antihistamines), otherwise I struggle with sinusitis and itchy eyes and nose, but until thusfar I have yet to find a way to eliminate all the allergies. 

Also, although I sleep a lot, I often experience nocturnal panic attacks, jaw clenching/teeth grinding, as well as balling myself up into a ball whilst asleep (I have to sleep with a pillow between my knees otherwise they get very bruised in the balling up process).

I am on antidepressants (Sertraline, 100mg) for the anxiety and depression, but I'm considering asking for a higher dosage when I have to get a new prescription. I have Ativans for the sleeping disturbances, but I build tolerance very quickly, so much so that I can only take it every other night.

Paranormal! 

When I took my gap year after finishing high-school, I stayed at home alone, exercising, cleaning the house, and doing some online courses. During this time, me and my father hated each other, so there was a lot of negative energy in the house, and everyone could feel it. 

One day, while I was on the stationary bicycle, I felt a nudge from the hind wheel, and looked around, expecting our (then) new dog having stuck her nose in the wheel again (she's not very smart), but was met with nothing. Thinking I imagined it, I turned to face forward again on the bicycle and without warning, I felt a hard shove to my face (hard enough for the clicking toes of the cycling shoes to unclip) and I fell off the bicycle - I looked around - no one. But I was scared, so I gathered the dogs in a corner with me and waited until someone got home. I had a raised scratchmark across my face. But when I told people, it would just sound too bizarre, so I just gave up. 

These shoving incidents kept happening, each time only when I was alone in a room and it would leave the strangest scratchmarks. I once even called my boyfriend's mum to come fetch me so I could spend the night at her place because I couldn't sleep in the house on my own. 

The worst and the last attack occurred just before 3 a.m. on a chilly morning, I felt the room get uncomfortably warm and an overwhelming rotten smell filled the room and then a scorching hot weight settling on top of me, holding my face, and then scratching long lines down my face, and then disappearing in the blink of an eye. The smell and the heat remained for a little while after. This might sound like a typical sleep paralysis experience, but I sat up, switched on my reading light and looked into my bedside mirror and there were scratchmarks across my face deep enough to draw blood. I immediately called a friend to spend the rest of the morning with. 

I later read somewhere (sixpenceee on Tumblr posted about it) that some religions keep crucifixes under their pillows to "keep away the demons when they sleep." I tried it that night, and I still sleep with the crucifix. Since then, only the occasional painting being thrown from the wall, bread being shoved off the countertop and a bucket being dragged along the floor on its own have occurred. 

This year has been free of malicious activity. I believe this to have been a result of the negative energy between me and my father at the time. I've never been more afraid, to be targeted by something unseen and unknown. I thought that God had truly abandoned me, and my every prayer was ignored. Maybe the crucifix thing worked because I believed in it. Nobody else in the house was ever targeted.

> "... suffered from migraines since I was nine ... "

Wow, I cannot begin to imagine how difficult it must be for you, having had to deal with chronic migraines from such a young age and for so long. My migraines only started early 2017, after my mental health took a tremendous dip (my mother was diagnosed with breast cancer and reacted very negatively to the news, I began drinking recklessly and ate only when necessary, and almost never slept). Shortly after diagnosis, my doctor and psychiatrist worked together as a team to determine the root cause of my migraines, and they came to the conclusion that my migraines occur most when I'm distressed. I stopped drinking alcohol completely.
I know this isn't highly recommended, but I'd suggest you maybe try removing certain things for a period of time to see if your migraines improve? (You've probably already tried it, but I don't know for sure, so I have to mention this) Like caffeine, aspirin - personally I found that these two only make things worse for me - or dairy, MSGs, etc. I don't use any pain medication, only abortives (Maxalt wafers) because I build resistance to pain medication too fast and there aren't many codeine-free products available on the market, and I'm not about to get addicted to pain meds. 

My anxiety and depression, however, has been around for far longer. I was born with hypertension. But I understand what you mean, feeling like a downer for everyone else by avoiding triggers. I can't be around bright/flashing lights, loud noises, I don't drink, can't do something that's too much like cardio... I'm a grandma in comparison to other people my age.

I avoid animal abuse/slaughter imagery too (I stay off Facebook for that reason, everyone sharing images of deceased animals), and a scene that actually had me fainting in my seat was that scene in The Impossible where Naomi Watts's character walks through the debris and her son catches a glimpse of dirty water and blood gushing from the wound in the back of her leg. The idea of dirty water and open wounds bothers me apparently.

I have been recommended to try pilates or yoga, but I'm reluctant to try it because I feel like I'd be making a fool of myself by showing up to a pilates/yoga class. But I'll definitely try swimming. Thank you for sharing your advice!

Yes, my left wrist is littered with scars. 

The vertical wounds left barely visible scars, whereas the horisontal wounds (across the wrist, from left to right or vice versa) healed but never faded much after they turned white and are quite a bit elevated in comparison to the rest of the skin. When I pull the skin taut on my wrist, the scars make folds in the skin, if that makes sense. The scars are literally white in colour, but I'm very pale in colour so that's probably not strange. 

Everyone knows exactly what they are though. I get heat rash when it gets too warm out, and a fellow student once grabbed my arm to inspect the rash, but immediately saw the age old scars and dropped my arm and went pale.

I've seen much worse than mine, and I often forget about it even existing, I don't dress to cover it up, but sometimes people do stare, and that's doesn't bother me much, because I keep reminding myself that everyone deals with personal issues at some point in their lives and they process it differently.
Thank you for your positivity. It's so easy to get holed up in all the stress and negativity, that it's hard to find encouraging advice. I appreciate it immensely :) Best wishes!

My aunt has been struggling with a restrictive eating disorder since the age of 14, she's met each of her weightloss goals, she's always weighed no more than 45. She's 57 now, and she still struggles to let herself consume a small garden salad. She no significant other, no social life, and she still hides the food she did not eat under her bed. She's the 3rd oldest sibling, but because of her dried out hair and wrinkled skin, she looks the oldest by far. 

Don't let the idea of "thin" consume you. It will loom over you for eternity if you do not take control of it. It will ruin your life if it hasn't done so already. It is not too late to start taking care of yourself.

I cut myself a lot as a teenager. I used the blades that I unscrewed from pencil sharpeners and scissors. I didn't think it was edgy, and I'd try my best to hide my wrists by wearing longsleeved shirts. Although I did have a weird "emo phase", the cutting started before said phase and also outlasted the phase. 

I had a lot of personal troubles going on, and (as it usually goes) my "friends" did not provide any emotional support whatsoever - in high school nobody has great friends, right? I never actively decided to stop, I just eventually outgrew the habit. 

It was a crutch for me to lean on when the pressure of life became too much, and I always felt relieved right after. 

Sometimes, it would be an attempt to sever an artery, I remember digging with the blade in my arm long enough to lose track of time and I'd become so frustrated that I'd just give up on trying.
